note: PASS WITH CAVEATS. (1) SOURCE. Item text comes from the Your COVID-19 Risk project's own LimeSurvey question-definition spreadsheet (Google Sheets key 1B9TLM1ro2yxEmfzWo99T6w0XADLeeJVXPvnFoEc0-vc, worksheet 'en', sha256 117c49c7d82d4913884eba9959dbe45ea2da7e0ed49995ce085e3485e9a047b0 as fetched 2026-09-10), which is named in the taskSpecs list of the project's CC0 build script rendered at https://your-risk.com/v1-translation-results-limesurvey. Its 'id' column holds the literal raw LimeSurvey/CSV column names (AttExExAltruistic ...), which data/peters_2025_covid19_risk_dcts.py lower-cases after stripping the AttExEx prefix -- a number/name-preserving rename (core model s3 pattern 2), so all 16 IRW item codes reconstruct from the sheet's own ids with no order inference. (2) STRUCTURE. These are bipolar semantic-differential items: one shared stem plus an item-specific anchor pair, exactly as the RAA DCT dct:expAttitude_expectation_73dnt5z1 prescribes ('create an item stem that contains the target behavior, and anchors that express the extremes of the bidimensional scale'). item_text therefore holds the sheet's own subquestion_en, which is IDENTICAL for all 16 items; the item's referent is carried by option_text, not by the stem. instructions and section_prompt are blank because the source publishes no separate participant instruction for this block. (3) OPTIONS. The companion DMQ_scales sheet (key 1GFFeIrwW9KVZxRCr4QrmQcVKDc5aSRu6VI4oWdQVkvw, sha256 6f5e225e4d5048a27e5395be7ba2894ec7fb4288270588992c5afd513a78ecee) states the answer-code key outright: bi = codes 1..7 displayed (-3)..(3), uni = codes 1..5 displayed (1)..(5), code 0 = '(not applicable)' (dropped by the IRW script). So resp=1 is the bottom anchor and resp=max the top anchor by published key, not by inference. Only the two endpoints carry verbal labels; intermediate points are labelled with their display number only, so option_text is left blank there rather than padded. Note the display numbers are NOT the stored codes for bi items (stored 4 = displayed 0, the midpoint). (4) ANCHOR TEXT is taken from bottom_anchor_bare/top_anchor_bare rather than bottom_anchor_en/top_anchor_en, which are the same strings with the LimeSurvey answer code appended ('very normal (1)'); the parenthetical is a generation artifact, and stripping it is the only deviation from the sheet. (5) PIPED TEXT. '{{distRec}}' is the study's own placeholder, kept verbatim; it was substituted at runtime with the country's recommended physical distance ('1 metre', '1.5 metres', '2 metres', '2.5 metres', '1 to 1.5 metres', '1 to 2 metres', ... per the distRec sheet, key 1TUBtl3ZkHQPvobLYg-nx9XvxApAte7bSUuT5JJGa2_Q), so no single literal sentence is what every respondent read. (6) LANGUAGE. The IRW table pools ~21 LimeSurvey deployments across countries and 23 administered languages (cov_language in the response table records each respondent's). Only the English source wording is shipped, because one itemtext row cannot hold 23 administered versions; English is the project's own source language and one of the administered versions, not a substitute translation, so text_source=study_materials and the 'language' / '_translated' columns are omitted. The other 22 worksheets of the same sheet hold the administered translations if a per-language table is ever wanted. (7) STEP 3B. The table name matches: the sheet's raa_construct for all 16 AttExEx rows reads 'Experiential attitude belief expectation', i.e. the belief-strength (expectation) component, and the sibling AttExEv rows ('I prefer feeling ...') are the evaluation component that goes to peters_2025_att_exp_eval. (8) RIGHTS -- READ THIS, IT IS A JUDGEMENT CALL, NOT A CLEAN ALL-CLEAR. The instrument is the study team's own bespoke RAA belief items, not a commercially published scale, and no fee/permission/no-derivatives/no-redistribution clause attaches to the wording anywhere I could find. But the project's main repository README (https://gitlab.com/a-bc/your-covid-19-risk/-/raw/master/README.md, sha256 27b2f56ac04d9125d0ea34cfb587173914a0c8a813a60290f5be5b84dfa243aa, fetched 2026-09-10) says: 'We aim to release everything here under permissive licenses. However, we still need to iron out some things (e.g. how to prevent abuse of the logo). Therefore, for now, standard copyright applies to everything in this repository except: 1. R scripts (.Rmd files), which we license under CC0 ...; 2. Data sets (.csv files) ... public domain ... We aim to release most materials under licenses comparable to the CC-BY-NC-SA license.' I read this as NOT a block, for three reasons: the copyright default is expressly scoped to 'everything in this repository' and the item wording is not in that repository (it is in world-readable Google Sheets, generated and published by the CC0 .Rmd); 'we aim to release most materials under licenses comparable to CC-BY-NC-SA' is a triple-hedged forward-looking intention that grants nothing and conditions nothing, not a term reserving a right today; and bare copyright with no stated restriction is explicitly not a block under the irw#1945 test. The counter-reading is that CC-BY-NC-SA names a non-commercial term and the questionnaire wording is a 'material', which would make this a block. FLAGGED FOR BEN: this ruling governs all seven peters_2025_* itemtext tables from this deposit, so it should be settled once in instrument_rights_register.csv rather than per table. No register row was written here to avoid colliding with the parallel sibling agents.
public_note: These are bipolar semantic-differential items: all 16 share one stem ('Keeping at least {{distRec}} distance from others makes me feel ...') and differ only in their anchor pair, so item_text is identical across items and the item's actual content sits in option_text at resp=1 and resp=max. Only the endpoints were verbally labelled, so intermediate resp values carry no option_text; the 15 seven-point items were displayed to respondents as -3..+3 (stored 1..7, so stored 4 is the midpoint) and 'weird' was a five-point 1..5 item. '{{distRec}}' is the study's own placeholder for the country's recommended physical distance (1 metre, 1.5 metres, 2 metres, ...), and the tool was fielded in 23 languages; only the English source wording is shipped, with each respondent's language in cov_language.

The study's DMQs spreadsheet gives one row per LimeSurvey question with the question code in its own 'id' column, so the tie is a label match rather than an order inference; the IRW code is that id lower-cased after the ^At?tInEv prefix, with the build script's own dmqReplacements shortening applied (Respons->Rspns, Flip->Fl, etc.), and data/peters_2025_covid19_risk_dcts.py does that rename with no positional step. Re-deriving all 55 codes from the sheet is exactly one-to-one and onto against the live item set (0 either way), the shipped stem and both anchors equal that row's own fields 55/55, and the sheet's uni/bi scale_type predicts the live per-item resp_max 55/55. Recorded as paper_explicit rather than data_labels because the spreadsheet is a companion instrument-definition file, not the header row of the response export -- the codes are identical, but the distinction is worth keeping honest. (Sibling tables in this batch chose data_labels for the same source shape; the underlying evidence is the same either way.) STEP 3b: the instrument matches the table name and the dictionary Description ('Instrumental attitude items -- belief evaluation component (RAA)'). The 55 live codes are exactly the sheet's 58 'Instrumental attitude belief evaluation' rows minus the three the build script's DMQs_to_globally_eliminate vector removes (AttInEvFamilySafe, AttInEvChildFeel, AttInEvChildReject), and every stem is an evaluation-component stem ('I prefer to ...', 'I prefer to be ...'), not the paired expectation component, which is the sibling table peters_2025_att_instr_strength. CAVEAT 1 (ANCHOR NUMERALS STRIPPED, deliberately): the labels the tool actually rendered are the sheet's *_anchor_en fields, which append the displayed scale value to the wording -- 'save face (-3)' / 'lose respect (3)' for bipolar items and '... (1)' / '... (5)' for unipolar ones. IRW ships the sheet's own *_anchor_bare variant of the same anchor ('save face', 'lose respect'), because the trailing numeral is the scale position rather than administered wording and SKILL forbids padding a scale point with its own number. Consequence to record: the bipolar items were shown to respondents as a -3..+3 scale and are stored in IRW as 1..7, and that display range is not recoverable from the shipped option_text. Same choice as the sibling tables in this batch. CAVEAT 2 (INTERMEDIATE OPTIONS BLANK): only resp=1 and resp=max carry option_text. The build script assigns the intermediate codes labels from the DMQ_scales sheet that are bare numerals -- '(2)'..'(4)' unipolar, '(-2)'..'(2)' bipolar -- so those rows are correctly blank rather than padded. The instrument is a semantic-differential radiobutton scale with words only at the two poles. CAVEAT 3 (POOLED LANGUAGES): the tool was fielded in 22 languages across 21 country deployments and this table pools all of them (per-respondent language is in the response table's cov_language). English is the AUTHORING language, not a translation -- the sheet's *_en columns are the master text everything else was translated from -- so text_source=study_materials rather than translated_substitute, and no `language` column or `_translated` columns are emitted. Respondents outside the English deployments read a translation of the shipped wording. CAVEAT 4 (AMENDED VARIANTS ARE NOT IN THIS TABLE): many countries received an amended wording, which the build script adds as a SEPARATE LimeSurvey question code (questionId + '2', e.g. AttInEvBi2). Those columns are absent from the processing script's ITEM_POLARITY dict, so the IRW table holds only original-wording responses and the sheet's original wording is the correct text for it. CAVEAT 5 (A SOURCE QUIRK, confirmed by the data): AttInEvBiFlip is named as the flipped twin of AttInEvBi but its spreadsheet row repeats its partner's anchors verbatim rather than swapping them -- the flip was never applied at the source. The live data agrees: bi M=1.403 and bifl M=1.396 (n=1130 / 1287), where a genuine flip would put bifl near 6.6. This is recorded as a property of the source instrument, not an IRW defect, and is below the issues-page bar (it is not a text-vs-table mismatch). NO INSTRUCTIONS OR SECTION PROMPT: the build script's add_group() call supplies no group description and DMQ_customizations' question_text column is entirely empty (parsed as col_logical()), so neither an instrument-level instruction nor a section prompt is published anywhere; both are left NA rather than invented. Single trivial section_id; correct_response NA (an attitude scale, no key). Items were shown as a randomised subset -- respondents chose how many items (0-20, in steps of 2) they were willing to answer -- which is why per-item n is ~1000-1330 rather than uniform.
